rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Diff pin 6d477099..HEAD renamed the Path 1/2/3 taxonomy in chunk 1 (lines 11-13, 'Path 1, connector inheritance.' / 'Path 2, `claude mcp add` from the command line.' / 'Path 3, first-party CLI via Bash.') and every later cross-reference to it — chunk 2 line 23 '`gh` CLI (Path 3, first-party CLI)', line 32 '(Path 1, connector inheritance, or Path 2, `claude mcp add`)', line 34 '(Path 2, `claude mcp add`)'; chunk 3 line 40 '(Path 1)'; chunk 7 line 110 '`claude mcp add`' — all resolve cleanly under the sequential-deck-read test: a reader who has read chunk 1 holds the Path N labels for every later use, and each later use even re-states the mechanism name rather than relying on the number alone. Closest borderline case, chunk 4 line 77: 'Cleanest UX of the three trackers for solo engineers, regardless of path.' — 'the three trackers' resolves against the GitHub Issues / Jira / Linear headers already read (chunks 2-4); 'path' (lowercase) resolves against the just-reused Path-N vocabulary. Also checked: line 5 'see the maintainer `Source verification` block' points past the `<!-- maintainer -->` cut (never rendered to students) but is citation-transparency an auditor reads, not a claim the student must resolve to use the page — stays PASS. No 'never named' or 'vague with full history' instance found in any of the 9 chunks.

No callback to another curriculum file anywhere in the body (all outbound doc-level pointers are external citation URLs with descriptive link text). Closest candidate, chunk 1 line 15 (unchanged region, only ', `claude mcp add`,' inserted by this diff): 'Per-tracker install commands come next. Plugins distribute Path 2, `claude mcp add`, at scale, under *Plugins and marketplaces* on this page.' — names the target section by its real title ('Plugins and marketplaces'), satisfying §2's 'name it, don't locate it' bar; 'on this page' scopes to the whole document rather than a relative position (not 'below'/'further down'), and 'come next' is a reading-order pointer, both within the carve-outs.

Z.'). `grep -niE 'one of the most|the best way|truly|game.?chang|revolutioniz' <file>` -> 0 matches (no self-grading superlative). Manual scan of all 9 chunks found no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no number+own-retraction pattern, no abstraction-noun stacks, no verb triplets with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -niE '\bcompendium\b|\bforcing function\b|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|\bsurface\b' <file>` hits only 'surface' as a noun, lines 48 and 70 (unchanged by this diff): 'only admins can add at this surface.' This is the ordinary engineering sense (install/attack-surface, a place in a system where something plugs in), not the repo's meta-dialect ('writing surface'); AE101's engineer-IC register and the compendium's own audience-register carve-out ('surface as ordinary engineering verb... NOT dialect') cover the adjacent noun usage here. None of 'compendium', 'forcing function', 'beat', 'mood' appear anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is a declared 'Flat lookup' (line 1) so the per-slide bold-count budget is off (§9 lookup-surface waiver) but the ≲5-word handle cap still binds, and bold placed mid-narrative is banned outright regardless of length. Scanned every `**...**` span in the body (word-count logic replicated from `check-slide-size.js`'s `stripInline`/`wordCount`, which drops backtick-code content before counting): only 3 spans exceed 5 words -- line 12 (6w, 'Path 2, `claude mcp add` from the command line.'), line 13 (6w, 'Path 3, first-party CLI via Bash.'), and line 60 (7w, 'individual engineers don't need per-install admin approval'). Lines 12-13 are the file's own core Path-1/2/3 taxonomy (this diff's whole point was to make these names cite-able from every later chunk per rule 1/2) -- trimming the bold to the number alone would sever the handle from the descriptive tag the rest of the document now points back at, degrading the artefact the diff just improved, so not filed. Line 60 is different in kind, not degree: it is bold placed mid-sentence on ordinary narrative/mechanism prose ('...and the domain is allowed, **individual engineers don't need per-install admin approval**. Admins control...'), which §9 bans outright ('Narrative... mechanism prose = no bold') independent of the word count. This exact specimen was already flagged in the prior slides-class instance at pin 6d477099 (five sibling instances in the same paragraph pattern were trimmed to true handles in this diff -- line 50 'CLI install', line 79 'Fallbacks', line 95 'Add a marketplace', line 23 'Default for AE101:', line 32 'When to add MCP instead.' -- but line 60 was not touched). Harm: on a lookup page a reader scans bold as the wayfinding cue to find their answer; a mid-paragraph emphasis clause that isn't a navigable entry point competes with the genuine section labels for the eye without functioning as one, which is exactly the finding-aid degradation §9's waiver exists to prevent.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Unbold line 60 entirely; the sentence reads fine as plain narrative and the true handle ('individual engineers') isn't a term anything else in the file cites back to.
